title: Two-sided platforms can stall at the cold-start tipping point
body:
Looking at five marketplace launches I have data on (rideshare, freelance, B2B parts).
[Step] Cohort tracking
  [Input] weekly GMV in months 1–18
[Step] Observation
  [Output] three of five never crossed the inflection where GMV growth becomes self-sustaining; two did
[Step] Pattern
  [Output] the survivors hand-curated one side of the market for the first ~6 months
The textbook two-sided-network story (each side attracts the other) only fires once both sides clear a threshold. Below threshold, the same dynamic works in reverse and the platform actively bleeds liquidity. This is not novel theory — it matches Rochet & Tirole — but my data hasn't ruled out selection effects in which platforms even agreed to share numbers with me.
